name: Bellhop hosting, configuration, startup, health and shutdown
description: What a node does from registration to shutdown: option handling, store selection, schema migration, node modes, the startup summary, the health check and graceful shutdown. Also holds product-level context (scope, principles, non-goals, phasing, design decisions) as info items. Job-level effects of shutdown live in the jobs module.

entities.name: Store
entities.description: The configured job store as seen by a node.

entities.name: Options
entities.description: Bellhop options after binding configuration and code.

entities.name: Health
entities.description: The result reported by the Bellhop health check on a node.

ears.shall: be a durable background-job library for .NET applications covering fire-and-forget, delayed and recurring jobs, continuations, chains and batches, retries, dead-lettering, cancellation and timeouts, multi-node execution over a shared store, a dashboard, observability and testing support

follow the product principles P1 to P9: three lines to a working system; one obvious way to define a job; correct under concurrency by construction; boring storage; secure and explicit by default; nothing is silent; testable without statics; trustworthy versioning and licensing; build in what everyone installs

requirements.notes: Every consequence listed in the principles table is restated by a concrete requirement elsewhere (P1: NFR-1; P2: TECH-14, TECH-15; P3: INV-103, INV-115, INV-203, TECH-51; P4: TECH-31, TECH-36, TECH-9, TECH-105; P5: REQ-301, INV-120, REQ-9; P6: NFR-51; P7: NFR-53, TECH-12, TECH-102; P8: NFR-20, NFR-37, NFR-18; P9: REQ-6). Kept here as context only.

ears.shall: define a job as data (a name plus a JSON document) with behaviour in a separate DI-constructed handler, so that renames, refactors and rolling deploys cannot break stored jobs

requirements.rationale: Answers the grievances in research.md §1.4 and §1.5; it is the pattern .NET developers know from MediatR, Wolverine, Brighter and MassTransit.

sources.quote: the stored record is a name plus a JSON document, so renames, refactors and rolling deploys cannot break it

ears.shall: not be a message bus, pub/sub system or cross-language job executor
not provide sagas, compensation, human-in-the-loop tasks or long-lived workflow state
offer no plugin API for third-party dashboard pages, job states or claim semantics; extension is through DI hooks and the JSON API only

requirements.rationale: ADR-3, decided by the project owner on 2026-11-03: the most-installed Hangfire plugin functionality is built in instead.

ears.shall: not offer exactly-once execution; delivery is at-least-once with idempotency tooling

not ship in v1: first-party MongoDB or MySQL stores, a hosted SaaS control plane, vendor-specific notification SDKs, remote execution agents, arbitrary script execution from the dashboard, Windows-specific features, or Hangfire's expression-based Enqueue(() => ...) API

requirements.notes: A Hangfire migration guide is promised (NFR-30). Whether a legacy adapter package ships is open (TECH-125).

ears.shall: stop the node from starting and report a message that names the option and the fix

sources.quote: Options MUST be validated at startup (ValidateOnStart) with messages that name the option and the fix.

ears.shall: treat job delivery as at-least-once: a job may start more than once within the duplicate window, which equals the lease length (LeaseDuration)

requirements.notes: Defined here because several modules rely on it; LeaseDuration itself is REQ-102 in the jobs module.

ears.shall: allow a node mode of Both, ClientOnly or WorkerOnly, with Both as the default (NodeMode)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: WorkerOnly runs workers and the scheduler but does not serve the dashboard (REQ-41). ClientOnly runs neither workers (REQ-20) nor the scheduler (REQ-40) and may serve the dashboard. Both does everything.

ears.shall: start the Bellhop node and only then connect to the store, check the schema and reconcile code-defined recurring jobs

sources.quote: Database connectivity, schema checks and job reconciliation happen in the hosted service, after the host starts.

ears.while: services are being registered and the host has not started
ears.shall: perform no I/O: no store connection, no schema check and no job reconciliation

ears.where: the process runs build-time tooling such as OpenAPI generation or EF Core design-time services
ears.shall: not start the scheduler or any worker
use the in-memory store

ears.if: no store is configured and the environment is not Development
ears.shall: log a warning that the in-memory store is in use

ears.where: an option is set both in configuration (the Bellhop section) and in code
ears.shall: use the value set in code

sources.quote: All options MUST be bindable from IConfiguration ("Bellhop": { ... }) and overridable in code.

ears.when: the store is reachable, the stored schema version is accepted (REQ-23, REQ-43) and all startup checks have passed
ears.shall: mark the node running and start the scheduler and the workers its mode allows

ears.when: the store is reachable, the stored schema version is accepted (REQ-23, REQ-43) and all startup checks have passed
ears.shall: log a one-screen summary with the store and schema version, the node mode, queues and concurrency, the registered job count, recurring jobs with their next run, and the dashboard path and auth mode

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-18 with a second consequence; the agent should model one action. The Redis store adds the server family to the summary (REQ-500). Secrets never appear in it (NFR-41).

ears.shall: never claim or execute a job on that node
default AutoMigrate to true in every environment (AutoMigrate)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (§9 Q4): true everywhere, as STO-3 says; the docs show the script export (TECH-47) on the first page.

ears.if: AutoMigrate is on and the stored schema version is older than the expected version
ears.shall: apply the embedded migrations up to the expected version and log what it did

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: concurrent starts are serialised by a store-side migration lock (REQ-42, TECH-126).

ears.if: AutoMigrate is off and the stored schema version is more than one version older than the expected version
ears.shall: stop the node from starting with a message that includes the path of the migration script

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a node accepts the schema version it expects or one version older, so library N+1 runs on schema N as STO-5 and NFR-18 require. A newer schema is REQ-43. Migrations therefore stay additive within a major version (TECH-127).

sources.quote: a version mismatch MUST fail fast at startup with the script path in the message

ears.when: a migration that is already applied is applied again
ears.shall: leave the schema unchanged

sources.quote: Migrations are embedded, versioned and idempotent.

ears.shall: keep retrying the connection with backoff without stopping the host, and claim no job until the store is reachable

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: Bellhop runs inside the application's host, so a database outage must not take the web application down. The health check reports Unhealthy meanwhile (REQ-31). The docs should advise mapping Bellhop health to readiness, not liveness, or the orchestrator restarts the pod in a loop.

ears.if: the node's clock differs from the database clock by more than ClockSkewThreshold
ears.shall: log a warning that names the measured skew

sources.quote: Bellhop MUST warn when node clock skew exceeds a threshold.

ears.shall: stop claiming new jobs on that node
give in-flight jobs ShutdownTimeout to finish after the host stops, 30 seconds by default (ShutdownTimeout)

ears.when: every in-flight job has finished, or ShutdownTimeout has passed and the remaining jobs' tokens were cancelled and their leases released
ears.shall: stop the node

requirements.notes: The job side (cancel token, release lease, job returns to Enqueued) is REQ-140 in the jobs module.

ears.if: an internal error stalls processing (store error, scheduler error, serialization error or recovery error)
ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

sources.quote: An error that would stall processing MUST also flip the health check.

ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

ears.if: the stored schema version is neither the expected version nor one version older
ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

requirements.notes: Follows from the accepted range (REQ-23): once the first N+1 node migrates during a rolling deploy, nodes still on N see a newer schema and report Unhealthy until they are replaced. They keep working meanwhile because migrations are additive (TECH-127).

ears.if: the node's worker loop is not alive
ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

ears.if: no check that reports Unhealthy fails, and scheduling lag exceeds SchedulingLagThreshold, dead-letter growth exceeds DeadLetterGrowthThreshold or failures in the window exceed FailureThreshold
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: backlog and failure checks give Degraded; MinNodesAlive gives Unhealthy (REQ-44). From Unhealthy as well, so a node whose store comes back but still has a backlog drops to Degraded instead of staying Unhealthy until the backlog clears.

ears.if: every check has passed on the last HealthyAfterPasses runs in a row
ears.shall: report the node Healthy

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: recovery needs consecutive passes so the status does not flap near a threshold. The source only implies recovery.

ears.shall: be delivered in three milestones: M1 core preview (job model, IJobClient, in-memory and PostgreSQL stores, fire-and-forget, delayed and recurring jobs, retries and dead letters, leases and recovery, OpenTelemetry, health check, Bellhop.Testing, read-only dashboard); M2 1.0 (SQL Server, SQLite and Redis stores, continuations, chains and batches, unique and concurrency keys, the full dashboard, BLT-1 to BLT-12, EF Core enqueue, analyzers, conformance suite, docs, benchmark); M3 1.x (BLT-13 to BLT-19, Tier 2 Redis-compatible servers, Garnet fixture, CLI, Native AOT verification, community stores)

requirements.notes: Items in every module carry an M1/M2/M3 tag where the phasing table places them.

ears.shall: record ownership in the store with an expiry rather than as mutual exclusion held by a live connection, and therefore not build on a distributed-lock library

requirements.rationale: ADR-1: claims, leases, recurring triggers, overlap and concurrency keys are all store-side atomic operations; a lock would add a round-trip, hide ownership from the dashboard and recovery, and reproduce Hangfire's lock-timeout failures. The technology constraint is TECH-51.

ears.shall: build the Redis store on sorted sets, lists, hashes and Lua scripts rather than Redis Streams

requirements.rationale: ADR-2: portability across Garnet, Dragonfly, Kvrocks and Upstash; Streams do not model delay, priority or uniqueness; deleting before ack needs Redis 8.2; a lease sorted set gives the same crash recovery. Constraints are TECH-54 and TECH-55.

ears.shall: cover several popular Hangfire add-ons through existing features rather than separate ones: multi-app shared store (namespaces), skip missed runs (misfire Skip), idempotency (unique keys) and options from configuration; jobs addressed by type-name strings are deliberately unsupported
not promote scheduled jobs, trigger recurring jobs or recover expired leases on that node

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (meaning of the node modes).

ears.shall: not serve the dashboard on that node

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (meaning of the node modes). Still open: whether mapping the dashboard on a WorkerOnly node fails startup or is ignored with a warning.

ears.when: several nodes start at the same time against a store whose schema is older than expected
ears.shall: let only the node holding the store's migration lock apply migrations, and have the others wait for the lock and then re-read the schema version

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. The lock lives in the store (TECH-126), consistent with ADR-1 and TECH-51.

ears.if: the stored schema version is newer than the expected version
ears.shall: stop the node from starting with a message that names both versions and says the library is older than the schema

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a node accepts its expected schema or one version older, never a newer one, whether AutoMigrate is on or off. During a rolling deploy a node on N that restarts after an N+1 node migrated fails here; that is acceptable because it is being replaced.

ears.if: fewer than MinNodesAlive nodes are alive
ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Every node reports this at the same moment, so an orchestrator that restarts on Unhealthy restarts the whole cluster together; the docs should say so.

ears.shall: default ClockSkewThreshold to 5 seconds (ClockSkewThreshold)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06; the source asks for a threshold but gives no value.

ears.shall: default SchedulingLagThreshold to 60 seconds (SchedulingLagThreshold)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06; the source says the thresholds are configurable but gives no defaults.

ears.shall: default DeadLetterGrowthThreshold to 100 dead-lettered jobs in 15 minutes (DeadLetterGrowthThreshold)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: default FailureThreshold to 50 failed attempts in 5 minutes (FailureThreshold)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: default MinNodesAlive to 1 (MinNodesAlive)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. The reporting node is itself alive, so the default never fires; applications opt in by raising it.

ears.shall: default HealthyAfterPasses to 3 (HealthyAfterPasses)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

scenarios.title: No store in Production falls back to memory, loudly
scenarios.given: A node starts in the Production environment with no store configured and valid options.
scenarios.then: The node is Running on the in-memory store and exactly one warning about it was logged.

scenarios.title: Invalid option stops startup
scenarios.given: A node starts with PollInterval set to a negative value in configuration.
scenarios.then: The node is StartupFailed, the message names PollInterval and the fix, and no job was claimed.

scenarios.title: Schema mismatch stops startup
scenarios.given: A node starts with AutoMigrate off and a store whose schema is two versions behind.

steps.note: node tries to start workers anyway

scenarios.title: Graceful shutdown
scenarios.given: A running node has two in-flight jobs; one finishes within ShutdownTimeout and one ignores cancellation.

steps.note: timeout passes, the remaining job's token is cancelled and its lease released

scenarios.then: The node is Stopped, it claimed nothing after the host stopped, and the second job is available to other nodes.

scenarios.title: Rolling deploy: new node runs on the previous schema
scenarios.given: Library version N+1 starts with AutoMigrate off against a store on schema version N; the store is reachable and options are valid.
scenarios.then: The node is Running on schema N and no migration was applied.

scenarios.title: Store down at startup keeps the host up
scenarios.given: A node starts while the database is unreachable.
scenarios.then: The host is still running, the node is Starting and reports Unhealthy, and no job was claimed.

glossary.ShutdownTimeout: Time in-flight jobs get to finish after the host stops; 30 s by default (REQ-28).
glossary.AutoMigrate: Whether a node applies embedded schema migrations at startup; true by default (REQ-21).
glossary.ClockSkewThreshold: Node-versus-database clock difference above which a warning is logged; 5 s by default (REQ-45).
glossary.SchedulingLagThreshold: Scheduling lag above which the node reports Degraded; 60 s by default (REQ-46).
glossary.DeadLetterGrowthThreshold: Dead-letter growth above which the node reports Degraded; 100 in 15 min by default (REQ-47).
glossary.FailureThreshold: Failed attempts in the window above which the node reports Degraded; 50 in 5 min by default (REQ-48).
glossary.MinNodesAlive: Live nodes below which every node reports Unhealthy; 1 by default (REQ-49).
glossary.HealthyAfterPasses: Consecutive passing health runs needed to return to Healthy; 3 by default (REQ-50).
glossary.LeaseDuration: How long a claim stays valid without a heartbeat; defined in the jobs module (REQ-102).
